text: [warm] Good morning, Kit! It's Captain Ada, calling from Moon Base. While I'm away, you are in charge of Starbase Nine! [chuckles] Orby will help you. Today, say hello to our visitor in the Docking Bay, and fix the lights in the Star Garden. Have fun, Station Keeper! [long pause] [cheerful] Good morning, Kit! Orby says you heard spooky noises last night. A ghost, on my station? [laughs] Well, keep your eyes open! Today the famous singer Madame Gloobella is docking, and the Snack-O-Tron in the Galley is broken. Can't have a station without snacks! [long pause] [warm] Morning, Kit! Captain Snorkel is bringing us a load of space ice today. The telescope in the Observatory is all mixed up. And Kit... the radio picked up a strange humming last night. Will you listen to the radio log? [long pause] [curious] Good morning, Kit! Professor Quasar is visiting today. He is very clever. Maybe he can help with our little ghost problem! And the fuses in the Engine Room keep blowing. [sighs] What a week!

[excited] Kit! Blip and Blop are visiting today, so hold on to your helmet! And I think you are very close to solving the mystery. Look at your clues in your Notebook. I believe in you! [long pause] [proud] Oh, Kit! You kept the station running, you answered every question, and you helped a little lost Glimmerling find her way home. You are the best Station Keeper Starbase Nine has ever had!

[excited] Beep boop! Hi Kit, I'm Orby! Tap on things to look at them. And if you ever get stuck, tap me for a hint! [long pause] Our visitor is waiting in the Docking Bay! Let's go say hello. [long pause] The lights in the Star Garden are out. Let's look at the light panel on the wall! [long pause] The Snack-O-Tron in the Galley needs fixing. Let's go! [long pause] The telescope in the Observatory is all mixed up. Let's fix it! [long pause] The fuse box in the Engine Room keeps sparking. Let's take a look! [long pause] Something is glowing on the floor of the Star Garden. Let's look! [long pause] Hmm, I think somebody has been in the cookie jar in the Galley! [long pause] Let's listen to the radio log on the comms console, on the Command Deck. [long pause] I heard munching in the Engine Room. Let's check the power cables on the floor!

Let's try the Glow-o-Meter in Crew Quarters. Ghost tracks might show up on the floor! [long pause] The telescope works again! Let's look at the star chart on the desk in the Observatory. [long pause] We have all six clues! Tap the Notebook and let's solve the mystery. [long pause] A hungry ghost needs a snack! Let's make a Glow Cookie with the Snack-O-Tron in the Galley. [long pause] The glowing footprints went into the air vent in Crew Quarters. Let's follow them! [long pause] Wisp needs to call home. Let's use the comms console on the Command Deck! [long pause] [yawns] All our jobs are done! Time for bed, Kit. Your bunk is in Crew Quarters. [long pause] Let's finish this first, then I can help! [long pause] [softly] Great job today, Kit. Good night, and sweet dreams! [long pause] [alarmed] Uh oh! The lights in the Star Garden just went out! The plants need their light!

[alarmed] Oh no! The Snack-O-Tron is out of power. No snacks! [long pause] [alarmed] Whoa! The telescope got all mixed up. It can't find the planets! [long pause] [alarmed] Zap! The fuse box in the Engine Room is sparking! [long pause] Connect each wire to the plug with the same colour! [long pause] The Snack-O-Tron needs just the right power. Pick batteries that add up to the number on the screen! [long pause] Put the planets back in order, starting with the one closest to the Sun! [long pause] Watch the fuse lights blink, then tap them in the same order! [long pause] Wisp will hum her mama's song. Tap the stars in the same order to send it out to space! [long pause] Hmm, not that one yet. Which planet comes next? [long pause] Oops! Let's watch again.

Too much power! Let's take a battery out. [long pause] [cheering] You fixed it! Great job, Kit! [long pause] [happy] Ding ding! Good as new! [long pause] [excited] Woo-hoo! You're a super fixer! [long pause] [gasps] Glowing goo! It's sticky, and it sparkles like starlight. Let's put it in the Notebook. [long pause] [surprised] The cookie jar is empty! Just crumbs... and a bit of that glowing goo again. Who ate all the cookies? [long pause] Look! This cable has tiny bite marks. Something has been nibbling the electricity! [long pause] [whispers] Listen... it's humming. Woo-ooo... mama... It sounds sad, not scary. [long pause] [excited] The Glow-o-Meter shows tiny glowing footprints! They go right into the air vent! [long pause] Look at this star chart! The Glimmer Nebula is full of little creatures made of light, called Glimmerlings. And they love to eat electricity!

Hmm, nothing new here right now. [long pause] It's too dark to see anything. Let's fix the lights first! [long pause] [nervous] D-did you hear that? [long pause] [scared] Eek! The lights are flickering! [long pause] [whispers] Was that... a ghost? [long pause] Wow! From up here, the Earth looks like a big blue marble. [long pause] [giggles] The captain's chair! It spins! Wheee! [long pause] Boxes and boxes of space socks. Why do we have so many socks? [long pause] Spaceships park right outside this window. Whoosh! [long pause] The airlock! Visitors come in here. Never open it without a spacesuit!

These space plants make fresh air for the whole station. [long pause] A moon melon! It grows super big in low gravity. [long pause] Lunch in space! Don't let your peas float away. [long pause] Freeze-dried ice cream! Crunchy and yummy. [long pause] The reactor core makes power for the whole station. Hummmm. [long pause] These pipes carry water and air all around the station. [long pause] A model of the planets. Eight planets going around the Sun! [long pause] A poster of the solar system. Can you find Saturn? It has rings! [long pause] Your toy rocket collection! Three, two, one, blast off! [long pause] Your Space Book! Every fact you learn goes in here.

Your cozy bunk! But it's not bedtime yet. We still have jobs to do. [long pause] [nervous] An air vent. It's dark in there. Brrr! [long pause] Let's make the Glow Cookie first. A hungry ghost likes a snack! [long pause] The comms console. This is how we talk to Captain Ada. [long pause] Nobody is here right now. [long pause] Our visitor is resting before the trip home. [long pause] The telescope can see all the way to the Glimmer Nebula now! [long pause] This is working just fine now! [long pause] Let's solve the mystery! Answer three questions. Use your clues! [long pause] What has the ghost been eating? Moon rocks? Cookies and electricity? Or space socks?

Where has the ghost been hiding? In the air vents? In the telescope? Or in the fridge? [long pause] What is the ghost, really? A spooky skeleton? A robot in a bedsheet? Or a lost baby Glimmerling? [long pause] Hmm, look at your clues again! [long pause] Yes! That matches the clues! [long pause] [excited] We solved it! The ghost is a lost baby Glimmerling, hiding in the air vents! Let's make her a snack and go say hello. [long pause] We need more clues before we can solve the mystery. [long pause] A Glow Cookie! Sparkly, crunchy and full of starlight. Perfect for a hungry Glimmerling. [long pause] [whispers] Shh... there's a little nest in here. Let's put the Glow Cookie down and wait. [long pause] [kindly] Don't worry, little one. We'll help you call your mama! [long pause] [excited] The song is going out to space! Look out the window!

[happy] What an adventure! Beep boop. Best friends forever, Kit! [long pause] Saturn's rings are made of chunks of ice and rock. Some are as small as a grain of sand, and some are as big as a house! [long pause] Jupiter is the biggest planet. More than a thousand Earths could fit inside it! [long pause] Mars looks red because its dusty ground has rusty iron in it. [long pause] Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun. A year on Mercury is only 88 days long! [long pause] The Sun is a star! It is the closest star to Earth, so it looks big and bright. [long pause] A constellation is a group of stars that makes a pattern, like Orion the Hunter or the Big Dipper. [long pause] Stars twinkle because the moving air around Earth bends their light. Out here in space, they don't twinkle at all! [long pause] Our galaxy is the Milky Way. It has hundreds of billions of stars! [long pause] A comet is like a dirty snowball of ice and dust. Near the Sun, it grows a long glowing tail.

Neil Armstrong walked on the Moon in 1969. His footprints are still there, because the Moon has no wind to blow them away! [long pause] The Moon is always round. As it travels around Earth, we see more or less of its sunny side. These are called phases. [long pause] The Moon takes about a month to go around the Earth. That's where the word month comes from! [long pause] Gravity pulls things toward each other. It keeps us on Earth, and it keeps Earth going around the Sun. [long pause] The station and everyone in it are falling around the Earth together, so everything floats. It's called free fall! [long pause] Sound needs air to travel. Space has almost no air, so it is very, very quiet out there. [long pause] The Moon doesn't make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it, like a mirror. [long pause] A spacesuit gives astronauts air to breathe and keeps them warm, cool and safe. [long pause] Rockets burn lots of fuel and push hot gas down very fast. That pushes the rocket up, up and away!

We live on Earth, the third planet from the Sun. It's the only planet we know of with living things. [long pause] There are eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

[shy] H-hello? Is that... a cookie? For me? [long pause] [sniffles] I'm sorry I ate your cookies, and your wires. I got lost, and I was so hungry... and I miss my mama. [long pause] [happy giggle] Really? Thank you, thank you! [long pause] [softly] This is my mama's song. Hmm, hmm-hmm, hmmm! [long pause] [happy] Bye bye, Kit! Bye bye, Orby! I'll never forget you!
[warm, echoing] Wisp! My little light! There you are. Thank you, kind Station Keeper. [long pause] [gently] Please take this star from our nebula. Whenever it shines, think of us.

[excited] Greetings, Earth kid! I am Zorp, from the planet Glorp! I came all this way to see the planets. But first... a quiz! Glorpians love quizzes! [long pause] [delighted] Correct-a-mundo! You are so smart! [long pause] Ooh, not quite! Try again, my friend. [long pause] [mysterious] Thank you, Earth kid! Oh, and last night I saw something glowing float past my window. Spooky! Bye-bye! [long pause] Which planet has the biggest, brightest rings? Is it... Saturn? Mars? Or Venus? [long pause] Which planet is the biggest of them all? Is it... Earth? Jupiter? Or Mercury? [long pause] Which planet is called the Red Planet? Is it... Neptune? Jupiter? Or Mars? [long pause] Which planet is closest to the Sun? Is it... Mercury? Saturn? Or Uranus?

[dramatic] Darling! It is I, Madame Gloobella, the brightest star in the galaxy! The stars are my audience, so let us talk about... stars! [long pause] [sings] Brava! Bravissima! [long pause] Oh no, no, no, darling. Try again! [long pause] [whispers] Before I go, darling... I heard someone singing in your air vents. Such a sad little song. Ta-ta! [long pause] What is our Sun? Is it... A planet? A star? Or A moon? [long pause] What do we call a group of stars that makes a picture in the sky? Is it... A constellation? A comet? Or A crater? [long pause] Why do stars twinkle when we look at them from Earth? Is it... They blink on and off? They are shy? Or The air bends their light? [long pause] We live in a giant spiral of stars. What is it called? Is it... The Big Swirl? The Milky Way? Or The Candy Bar?

[hearty laugh] Ho ho! Captain Snorkel here, with a load of fresh space ice! Answer my questions while I unload, kiddo. [long pause] [laughs] Ho ho! That's right, kiddo! [long pause] Whoops! Not that one. Have another go. [long pause] Be careful, kiddo. Last time I docked here, my lunchbox went all glowy and somebody ate my sandwich! Ho ho! Keep on truckin'! [long pause] What is a comet mostly made of? Is it... Fire? Cheese? Or Ice and dust? [long pause] Who was the first person to walk on the Moon? Is it... Neil Armstrong? Captain Snorkel? Or A cow? [long pause] Why does the Moon seem to change shape every night? Is it... Someone takes a bite? We see different parts of its sunny side? Or It shrinks in the wash? [long pause] About how long does the Moon take to go all the way around the Earth? Is it... One hour? One hundred years? Or About a month?

[curious] Ah! Professor Quasar, scientist extraordinaire. A ghost, you say? Fascinating! Answer my questions, and I shall lend you my newest invention. [long pause] Excellent! Precisely correct! [long pause] Hmm, no, no. Think again, young scientist. [long pause] [proud] Take my Glow-o-Meter! It shows things that glow, even when your eyes cannot see them. Ghost hunting! Ha! Good luck! [long pause] What pulls things down and keeps your feet on the ground? Is it... Gravity? Magnets? Or Glue? [long pause] Why do astronauts float inside a space station? Is it... They are full of balloons? They are falling around Earth with the station? Or They forgot their shoes? [long pause] Can you hear sounds out in empty space? Is it... Yes, it is very loud? Only on Tuesdays? Or No, there is no air to carry sound? [long pause] Where does moonlight really come from? Is it... Sunlight bouncing off the Moon? Giant moon lamps? Or Glowing moon bugs?

[giggles] Hi! I'm Blip! And I'm Blop! We love rockets! Do you love rockets? Quiz time! [long pause] [cheering] Yay! Woo-hoo! You got it! [long pause] Nope, nope! Try again! [long pause] [whispers] Psst! We saw a teeny glowy baby in your air vent! It looked sad! Bye! Bye! [long pause] What do astronauts wear to stay safe outside the station? Is it... Pajamas? A spacesuit? Or A raincoat? [long pause] What makes a rocket blast off into space? Is it... Burning fuel pushing gas down? A big trampoline? Or A really strong sneeze? [long pause] Which planet do people live on? Is it... Pluto? Neptune? Or Earth? [long pause] How many planets go around our Sun? Is it... Three? Eight? Or Fifty?
